name: "PostgreSQL Gateway Tests (seaweed-mono)"
# The dispatch inputs ride in the run name so the runner watchdog
# (runner-watchdog.yml) can cancel a run stuck on an offline tp01 and
# re-dispatch it on hosted with the same inputs. Keep the fields parseable:
# mono:<sha> branch:<ref> runner:<tp01|hosted>.
run-name: ${{ github.workflow }}${{ (github.event.client_payload.sha || inputs.mono_sha) && format(' · mono:{0}', github.event.client_payload.sha || inputs.mono_sha) || '' }} · branch:${{ github.event.client_payload.ref || inputs.gitlab_branch || 'main' }} · runner:${{ inputs.runner || 'hosted' }}

on:
  # Triggered by seaweed-mono push (repository_dispatch)
  repository_dispatch:
    types:
      - mono-push
      - mono-merge-request

  # Allow manual triggering
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      gitlab_branch:
        description: 'seaweed-mono branch to test'
        required: false
        default: 'main'
      mono_sha:
        description: 'Exact seaweed-mono commit to test; defaults to the head of the branch above'
        required: false
        default: ''
      runner:
        description: 'Where to run: tp01 (self-hosted, no queue) or hosted (fallback when tp01 is down)'
        required: false
        type: choice
        default: hosted
        options: [tp01, hosted]
      measurement:
        description: 'Isolate this run from production: use a separate concurrency group so a real dispatch cannot cancel it'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  # head_ref is empty for repository_dispatch/workflow_dispatch, so key on the
  # dispatched mono ref (or the manual branch input) to actually dedupe runs.
  group: ${{ github.event.client_payload.ref || github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch || 'main' }}${{ inputs.measurement && '/measure' || '' }}/postgres-tests
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  postgres-basic-tests:
    name: PostgreSQL Basic Tests
    # Fixed host ports (9333 / 8888 / 8333 / 8000 / 5432) can be bound by only
    # one job at a time on a shared host, so on tp01 every port-binding job
    # across every suite takes the same single repository-wide slot. A hosted
    # runner is a fresh VM per job, so it gets a key unique to this job and
    # matrix leg and never waits.
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ (inputs.runner || 'hosted') == 'tp01' && 'tp01-host-ports' || format('hosted-{0}-{1}-{2}', github.run_id, 'postgres-basic-tests', strategy.job-index) }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ${{ (inputs.runner || 'hosted') == 'tp01' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","tp01"]') || fromJSON('["ubuntu-latest"]') }}
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
    - name: Checkout artifactory repo
      uses: actions/checkout@v6

    - name: Runner housekeeping (self-hosted only)
      uses: ./.github/actions/runner-housekeeping

    - name: Link to seaweed-mono source
      if: github.event_name == 'repository_dispatch'
      uses: ./.github/actions/mono-source-link

    - name: Clone seaweed-mono (enterprise) source
      uses: ./.github/actions/clone-mono-source
      with:
        token: ${{ secrets.MONO_TOKEN }}
        branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch }}
        sha: ${{ inputs.mono_sha }}

    - name: Set up Go 1.x
      uses: actions/setup-go@v6
      with:
        go-version-file: 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/go.mod'
        cache-dependency-path: 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/go.sum'
      id: go

    # Hosted-only: this rewrites the daemon config and restarts Docker, which on
    # a shared self-hosted host would clobber the operator's daemon.json and kill
    # any container the host is running. tp01 is not rate-limited by Docker Hub
    # the way a hosted runner's shared egress IP is, so it needs no mirror.
    - name: Configure Docker Hub mirror
      if: runner.environment == 'github-hosted'
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
      run: |
        echo '{"registry-mirrors": ["https://mirror.gcr.io"]}' | sudo tee /etc/docker/daemon.json
        sudo systemctl restart docker

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4

    - name: Cache Docker layers
      uses: actions/cache@v5
      with:
        path: /tmp/.buildx-cache
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-postgres-${{ github.sha }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-postgres-

    - name: Start PostgreSQL Gateway Services
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/postgres
      run: |
        make dev-start
        sleep 10

    - name: Run Basic Connectivity Test
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/postgres
      run: |
        make test-basic

    - name: Run PostgreSQL Client Tests
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/postgres
      run: |
        make test-client

    - name: Save logs
      if: always()
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/postgres
      run: |
        docker compose logs > postgres-output.log || true

    - name: Archive logs
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: postgres-logs-${{ env.COMMIT_SHA }}
        path: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/postgres/postgres-output.log

    - name: PostgreSQL Test Summary
      if: always()
      run: |
        echo "## 🐘 PostgreSQL Gateway Test Summary" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "### Source" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "- **Commit**: ${COMMIT_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "### Test Components" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "- 🔌 **Basic Connectivity**: PostgreSQL protocol compatibility" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "- 📊 **Client Tests**: Standard PostgreSQL client operations" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "- 🐳 **Docker Integration**: Containerized test environment" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "### PostgreSQL Gateway Features" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "- ✅ **Protocol Compatibility**: Standard PostgreSQL wire protocol" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "- ✅ **SQL Query Support**: Basic SQL operations over SeaweedFS" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "- ✅ **Client Library Support**: Works with standard PostgreSQL clients" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

    - name: Cleanup
      if: always()
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/postgres
      run: |
        make clean || true

jobs:
  rust-unit-tests:
    name: Rust Unit Tests
    runs-on: ${{ (inputs.runner || 'hosted') == 'tp01' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","tp01"]') || fromJSON('["ubuntu-22.04"]') }}
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
      - name: Checkout artifactory repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Runner housekeeping (self-hosted only)
        uses: ./.github/actions/runner-housekeeping

      - name: Link to seaweed-mono source
        if: github.event_name == 'repository_dispatch'
        uses: ./.github/actions/mono-source-link

      - name: Clone seaweed-mono (enterprise) source
        uses: ./.github/actions/clone-mono-source
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.MONO_TOKEN }}
          branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch }}
          sha: ${{ inputs.mono_sha }}

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Cache cargo registry and target
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume/target
          key: rust-${{ hashFiles('seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            rust-

      - name: Build Rust volume server
        run: cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume && cargo build --release

      - name: Run Rust unit tests
        run: cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume && cargo test

  rust-integration-tests:
    name: Rust Integration Tests
    runs-on: ${{ (inputs.runner || 'hosted') == 'tp01' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","tp01"]') || fromJSON('["ubuntu-22.04"]') }}
    timeout-minutes: 30

    steps:
      - name: Checkout artifactory repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Runner housekeeping (self-hosted only)
        uses: ./.github/actions/runner-housekeeping

      - name: Clone seaweed-mono (enterprise) source
        uses: ./.github/actions/clone-mono-source
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.MONO_TOKEN }}
          branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch }}
          sha: ${{ inputs.mono_sha }}

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/go.mod'

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Cache cargo registry and target
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume/target
          key: rust-${{ hashFiles('seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            rust-

      - name: Build Go weed binary
        run: |
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/weed
          go build -tags 5BytesOffset -o weed .
          chmod +x weed
          ./weed version

      - name: Build Rust volume binary
        run: cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume && cargo build --release

      - name: Run integration tests
        env:
          WEED_BINARY: ${{ github.workspace }}/seaweedfs-source/enterprise/weed/weed
          RUST_VOLUME_BINARY: ${{ github.workspace }}/seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume/target/release/weed-volume
        run: |
          echo "Running Rust volume server integration tests..."
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise
          go test -v -count=1 -tags 5BytesOffset -timeout=15m ./test/volume_server/rust/...

      - name: Collect logs on failure
        if: failure()
        run: |
          mkdir -p /tmp/rust-volume-server-it-logs
          find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "seaweedfs_volume_server_it_*" -print -exec cp -r {} /tmp/rust-volume-server-it-logs/ \; || true

      - name: Archive logs on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: rust-volume-server-integration-test-logs
          path: /tmp/rust-volume-server-it-logs/
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Test summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          echo "## Rust Volume Server Integration Test Summary" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "- Suite: test/volume_server/rust" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "- Command: go test -v -count=1 -tags 5BytesOffset -timeout=15m ./test/volume_server/rust/..." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  rust-volume-go-tests:
    name: Go Tests with Rust Volume (${{ matrix.test-type }} - Shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
    runs-on: ${{ (inputs.runner || 'hosted') == 'tp01' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","tp01"]') || fromJSON('["ubuntu-22.04"]') }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        test-type: [grpc, http]
        shard: [1, 2, 3]

    steps:
      - name: Checkout artifactory repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Runner housekeeping (self-hosted only)
        uses: ./.github/actions/runner-housekeeping

      - name: Clone seaweed-mono (enterprise) source
        uses: ./.github/actions/clone-mono-source
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.MONO_TOKEN }}
          branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch }}
          sha: ${{ inputs.mono_sha }}

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/go.mod'

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Cache cargo registry and target
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume/target
          key: rust-${{ hashFiles('seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            rust-

      - name: Build Go weed binary
        run: |
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/weed
          go build -tags 5BytesOffset -o weed .
          chmod +x weed
          ./weed version

      - name: Build Rust volume binary
        run: cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume && cargo build --release

      - name: Run volume server integration tests with Rust volume
        env:
          WEED_BINARY: ${{ github.workspace }}/seaweedfs-source/enterprise/weed/weed
          RUST_VOLUME_BINARY: ${{ github.workspace }}/seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume/target/release/weed-volume
          VOLUME_SERVER_IMPL: rust
        run: |
          if [ "${{ matrix.test-type }}" == "grpc" ]; then
            if [ "${{ matrix.shard }}" == "1" ]; then
              TEST_PATTERN="^Test[A-H]"
            elif [ "${{ matrix.shard }}" == "2" ]; then
              TEST_PATTERN="^Test[I-S]"
            else
              TEST_PATTERN="^Test[T-Z]"
            fi
          else
            if [ "${{ matrix.shard }}" == "1" ]; then
              TEST_PATTERN="^Test[A-G]"
            elif [ "${{ matrix.shard }}" == "2" ]; then
              TEST_PATTERN="^Test[H-R]"
            else
              TEST_PATTERN="^Test[S-Z]"
            fi
          fi
          echo "Running Go volume server tests with Rust volume for ${{ matrix.test-type }} (Shard ${{ matrix.shard }}, pattern: ${TEST_PATTERN})..."
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise
          go test -v -count=1 -tags 5BytesOffset -timeout=30m ./test/volume_server/${{ matrix.test-type }}/... -run "${TEST_PATTERN}"

      - name: Collect logs on failure
        if: failure()
        run: |
          mkdir -p /tmp/rust-volume-go-test-logs
          find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "seaweedfs_volume_server_it_*" -print -exec cp -r {} /tmp/rust-volume-go-test-logs/ \; || true

      - name: Archive logs on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: rust-volume-go-test-logs-${{ matrix.test-type }}-shard${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: /tmp/rust-volume-go-test-logs/
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Test summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ "${{ matrix.test-type }}" == "grpc" ]; then
            if [ "${{ matrix.shard }}" == "1" ]; then
              TEST_PATTERN="^Test[A-H]"
            elif [ "${{ matrix.shard }}" == "2" ]; then
              TEST_PATTERN="^Test[I-S]"
            else
              TEST_PATTERN="^Test[T-Z]"
            fi
          else
            if [ "${{ matrix.shard }}" == "1" ]; then
              TEST_PATTERN="^Test[A-G]"
            elif [ "${{ matrix.shard }}" == "2" ]; then
              TEST_PATTERN="^Test[H-R]"
            else
              TEST_PATTERN="^Test[S-Z]"
            fi
          fi
          echo "## Rust Volume - Go Test Summary (${{ matrix.test-type }} - Shard ${{ matrix.shard }})" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "- Suite: test/volume_server/${{ matrix.test-type }} (Pattern: ${TEST_PATTERN})" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "- Volume server: Rust (VOLUME_SERVER_IMPL=rust)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: "Volume Tiering Tests (seaweed-mono)"
# The dispatch inputs ride in the run name so the runner watchdog
# (runner-watchdog.yml) can cancel a run stuck on an offline tp01 and
# re-dispatch it on hosted with the same inputs. Keep the fields parseable:
# mono:<sha> branch:<ref> runner:<tp01|hosted>.
run-name: ${{ github.workflow }}${{ (github.event.client_payload.sha || inputs.mono_sha) && format(' · mono:{0}', github.event.client_payload.sha || inputs.mono_sha) || '' }} · branch:${{ github.event.client_payload.ref || inputs.gitlab_branch || 'main' }} · runner:${{ inputs.runner || 'hosted' }}

# End-to-end guard for the storage-class tiering DSL. A real cluster is driven
# both through `weed shell` and through the plugin worker (RunDetection ->
# ExecuteJob, the admin's path), and every assertion reads back the topology the
# worker itself plans from — not shell output.
#
# Two layouts run on separate runners:
#   single-disk  (make test)           two servers per medium, one disk each
#   multi-disk   (make test-multidisk) every server hosts both media
# The multi-disk layout is what proves a same-node cross-disk move still crosses
# to another node: the source node holds the target disk, and a node-wide delete
# would destroy the data if the move stayed local, so a passing move is the proof
# the source-node exclusion holds. It also exercises the same-ratio cross-medium
# EC shard relocation, which the single-disk layout cannot reach.

on:
  # Triggered by seaweed-mono push (repository_dispatch)
  repository_dispatch:
    types:
      - mono-push
      - mono-merge-request

  # Allow manual triggering
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      gitlab_branch:
        description: 'seaweed-mono branch to test'
        required: false
        default: 'main'
      mono_sha:
        description: 'Exact seaweed-mono commit to test; defaults to the head of the branch above'
        required: false
        default: ''
      runner:
        description: 'Where to run: tp01 (self-hosted, no queue) or hosted (fallback when tp01 is down)'
        required: false
        type: choice
        default: hosted
        options: [tp01, hosted]
      measurement:
        description: 'Isolate this run from production: use a separate concurrency group so a real dispatch cannot cancel it'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  # head_ref is empty for repository_dispatch/workflow_dispatch, so key on the
  # dispatched mono ref (or the manual branch input) to actually dedupe runs.
  group: ${{ github.event.client_payload.ref || github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch || 'main' }}${{ inputs.measurement && '/measure' || '' }}/volume-tiering
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  volume-tiering-tests:
    name: Volume Tiering E2E (${{ matrix.layout }})
    runs-on: ${{ (inputs.runner || 'hosted') == 'tp01' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","tp01"]') || fromJSON('["ubuntu-22.04"]') }}
    timeout-minutes: 40
    strategy:
      # Report both layouts independently; one failing must not cancel the other.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - layout: single-disk
            target: test
          - layout: multi-disk
            target: test-multidisk
    steps:
    - name: Checkout artifactory repo
      uses: actions/checkout@v6
      with:
        persist-credentials: false

    - name: Runner housekeeping (self-hosted only)
      uses: ./.github/actions/runner-housekeeping

    - name: Link to seaweed-mono source
      if: github.event_name == 'repository_dispatch'
      uses: ./.github/actions/mono-source-link

    - name: Clone seaweed-mono (enterprise) source
      uses: ./.github/actions/clone-mono-source
      with:
        token: ${{ secrets.MONO_TOKEN }}
        branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch }}
        sha: ${{ inputs.mono_sha }}

    # Branches predating the suite have no directory; branches predating the
    # multi-disk layout have the directory but no test-multidisk target. Skip
    # rather than fail so each layout only runs where it actually exists.
    - name: Check for the suite and this layout
      id: check
      run: |
        present=false
        dir=seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/volume_tiering
        if [ -d "$dir" ]; then
          if [ "${{ matrix.target }}" = "test-multidisk" ] && ! grep -qE '^test-multidisk:' "$dir/Makefile"; then
            echo "::notice::Branch has no test-multidisk target; skipping the multi-disk layout."
          else
            present=true
          fi
        else
          echo "::notice::Branch has no enterprise/test/volume_tiering; skipping."
        fi
        echo "present=$present" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    - name: Set up Go
      if: steps.check.outputs.present == 'true'
      uses: actions/setup-go@v6
      with:
        go-version-file: 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/go.mod'
        cache-dependency-path: 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/go.sum'

    # The suite's teardown waits for the cluster's ports to be released before a
    # following start, which it checks with lsof.
    # apt-retry.sh runs apt-get under sudo, and tp01's runner account has no
    # sudo at all, so this step can only run on a hosted image. lsof is already
    # installed on tp01 (/usr/bin/lsof) — keep it installed there.
    - name: Install lsof
      if: steps.check.outputs.present == 'true' && runner.environment == 'github-hosted'
      run: $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/apt-retry.sh update && $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/apt-retry.sh install -y lsof

    - name: Verify lsof is present (self-hosted)
      if: steps.check.outputs.present == 'true' && runner.environment != 'github-hosted'
      run: command -v lsof

    - name: Run volume tiering E2E suite (${{ matrix.layout }})
      if: steps.check.outputs.present == 'true'
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/volume_tiering
      run: make ${{ matrix.target }}

    - name: Collect cluster logs on failure
      if: failure()
      run: |
        mkdir -p /tmp/volume-tiering-logs
        find /tmp/volume_tiering_test -name '*.log' -exec cp --parents {} /tmp/volume-tiering-logs/ \; 2>/dev/null || true

    - name: Archive cluster logs on failure
      if: failure()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: volume-tiering-logs-${{ matrix.layout }}-${{ env.COMMIT_SHA }}
        path: /tmp/volume-tiering-logs/
        if-no-files-found: warn
        retention-days: 7

    - name: Stop the cluster
      if: always() && steps.check.outputs.present == 'true'
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/volume_tiering
      run: make stop || true

    - name: Summary
      if: always()
      run: |
        echo "## Volume Tiering E2E — ${{ matrix.layout }}" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        if [ "${{ steps.check.outputs.present }}" != "true" ]; then
          echo "Layout not present on this branch; skipped." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          exit 0
        fi
        echo "Result: **${{ job.status }}** (\`make ${{ matrix.target }}\`)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "Suite \`test/volume_tiering\`, driven through \`weed shell\` and the plugin worker against a live cluster; assertions read the observed topology." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        if [ "${{ matrix.layout }}" = "multi-disk" ]; then
          echo "### Multi-disk layout" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "- every server hosts both media, so a move from a node's ssd must still cross to another node's hdd_ht" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "- proves the same-node cross-disk refusal (a node-wide delete would destroy the data otherwise)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "- exercises the same-ratio cross-medium EC shard relocation" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  retag:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Login to Docker Hub

        with:

          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}

        with:

            for suffix in "" _full _large_disk _large_disk_full _large_disk_rocksdb _large_disk_rocksdb_9_3 _large_disk_foundationdb; do
              src="$image:$version$suffix"
              if docker buildx imagetools inspect "$src" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

            done
          done

  # End-to-end test for the versioned-EC vacuum 2PC switch protocol.
  # Drives a real local cluster (master + 14 volume servers + filer +
  # 2 workers + admin, all `weed` subprocesses on localhost ports) through
  # three sequential vacuum rounds:
  #   - round 1: 0 -> 1
  #   - round 2: 1 -> 2 (exercises post-switch reads, the path that the
  #     read-time Version + shard-fd-swap fix unblocks)
  #   - vacuum-to-empty (2 -> 3): empty new generation triggers the
  #     TeardownEmptyVolume callback cluster-wide.
  ec-vacuum-2pc-tests:
    name: EC Vacuum 2PC Switch Tests
    runs-on: ${{ (inputs.runner || 'hosted') == 'tp01' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","tp01"]') || fromJSON('["ubuntu-22.04"]') }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
    - name: Checkout artifactory repo
      uses: actions/checkout@v6

    - name: Runner housekeeping (self-hosted only)
      uses: ./.github/actions/runner-housekeeping

    - name: Clone seaweed-mono (enterprise) source
      uses: ./.github/actions/clone-mono-source

        token: ${{ secrets.MONO_TOKEN }}
        branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch }}
        sha: ${{ inputs.mono_sha }}

    - name: Set up Go 1.x
      uses: actions/setup-go@v6
      with:
        go-version-file: 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/go.mod'
        cache-dependency-path: 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/go.sum'
      id: go

    - name: Run EC Vacuum 2PC Switch Test
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/ec_vacuum/admin_dockertest
      env:
        EC_VACUUM_INTEGRATION: "1"
      run: |
        # The test forks ~18 weed subprocesses (master + 14 volume +
        # filer + 2 workers + admin) and drives the ec_vacuum plugin
        # through three sequential 2PC switch rounds. It builds its own
        # `weed_bin` from the source tree; the 30-minute job timeout
        # covers the ~6-8 minute happy-path run plus per-step deadlines
        # (5min waitForActiveVersion per round + cluster boot).
        echo "Running TestEcVacuumVersionedSwitch..."
        echo "  - round 1: active_version 0 -> 1 (stage / Prepare / Commit fan-out)"
        echo "  - round 2: 1 -> 2 (validates post-switch read path)"
        echo "  - vacuum-to-empty: 2 -> 3 + TeardownEmptyVolume across all 14 holders"
        # Anchored: the Rust variant of this scenario is its own job.
        go test -v -timeout 25m -run '^TestEcVacuumVersionedSwitch$' .

    - name: Archive test logs

      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: ec-vacuum-2pc-test-logs-${{ env.COMMIT_SHA }}

        retention-days: 7

    - name: EC Vacuum 2PC Test Summary
      if: always()
      run: |
        echo "## EC Vacuum 2PC Switch Test Summary" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "End-to-end integration test for the versioned-EC vacuum SwitchVersion protocol." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "See \`weed/worker/tasks/ec_vacuum/DESIGN.md\` for the protocol." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "### What This Exercises" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **stage / Prepare / Commit fan-out** across all 14 shard holders" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Master heartbeat propagation** of \`active_version\` / \`has_pending_switch\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Versioned-EC LookupEcVolume.VersionedLocations** populated and read by the worker" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Post-switch reads**: the commit handler refreshes \`ev.Version\` from \`.vif.v<N>\` and reopens shard / .ecx / .ecj fds; without this, post-switch reads tripped a one-byte 'size mismatch'." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Worker's compaction target version** stamped into the new \`.vif.v<N>\` (so the server-side refresh picks the right needle layout)." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Vacuum-to-empty TeardownEmptyVolume**: empty new generation removes the EcVolume from every shard holder's disk_location map and unlinks every \`<base>.*\` file." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "### What This Catches" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- Worker writing \`.vif.v<N>\` with the source's needle Version instead of the post-compaction one" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- \`OpenAgainstGeneration\` swapping \`.ecx\` / \`.ecj\` but leaving \`shard.ecdFile\` on legacy \`.ec<NN>\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

# The dispatch inputs ride in the run name so the runner watchdog
# (runner-watchdog.yml) can cancel a run stuck on an offline tp01 and
# re-dispatch it on hosted with the same inputs. Keep the fields parseable:
# mono:<sha> branch:<ref> runner:<tp01|hosted>.
run-name: ${{ github.workflow }}${{ (github.event.client_payload.sha || inputs.mono_sha) && format(' · mono:{0}', github.event.client_payload.sha || inputs.mono_sha) || '' }} · branch:${{ github.event.client_payload.ref || inputs.gitlab_branch || 'main' }} · runner:${{ inputs.runner || 'hosted' }}

# First wave of coverage for enterprise/test/s3tables, which no workflow in this
# repo referenced before. Two of these four suites run nowhere today; the other
# two run only in seaweedfs/seaweedfs, so an enterprise-side change to the
# catalog or the maintenance worker has no gate.
#
# Why these four first, out of twenty directories:
#
#   maintenance         Compaction, snapshot expiry, orphan removal. Runs in
#                       NEITHER repo today — upstream's s3-tables-tests.yml has
#                       no job for it. Cheapest suite here and the one guarding
#                       the worker that rewrites customer data.
#   lifecycle           The data-corruption gate. It exists because compaction
#                       once rewrote every dictionary-encoded column onto a
#                       single value while every maintenance test passed, since
#                       none of them opened the parquet the worker had written.
#                       It now checks row count, per-column dictionary
#                       cardinality, and an md5 over whole rows.
#   catalog_clickhouse  The manifest-repair gate from the positive side:
#                       ClickHouse's experimental Iceberg writer commits
#                       non-compliant manifests that the catalog repairs.
#   catalog_olake       The same gate from the negative side, plus two paths
#                       nothing else covers: a strict Java Iceberg client (OLake
#                       writes through a Java sidecar) and equality deletes
#                       (OLake is a CDC tool, so its upsert path emits them).
#
# Deliberately deferred, not forgotten — each needs an engine image and a
# topology this wave does not set up: catalog_spark, catalog_spark_lance,
# catalog_trino, catalog_dremio, catalog_doris, catalog_risingwave,
# catalog_lancedb, catalog_duckdb_lance, lakekeeper, polaris, unity_catalog,
# admin, catalog, sts_integration, table-buckets. Add them in a second wave
# rather than enabling a matrix that mostly skips.
#
# THE SKIP GUARD IS THE POINT, not decoration. Every suite under
# enterprise/test/ begins with a t.Skip() conditional on its environment being
# present, so a job that wires the suite without provisioning it reports green
# having tested nothing. That is worse than the status quo, because it replaces
# a known hole with an invisible one. Each run therefore asserts the suite
# actually executed: at least one --- PASS and no --- SKIP at the top level.

on:
  # DELIBERATELY MANUAL-ONLY ON FIRST MERGE. The repository_dispatch types that
  # every other enterprise suite listens on are commented out below, and a
  # follow-up PR restores them once this workflow has been proven by a manual
  # run.
  #
  # The reason is a GitHub constraint, not caution for its own sake:
  # workflow_dispatch only works for a workflow file that is already on the
  # default branch, so this file cannot be dispatched before it merges — the
  # API answers "workflow not found on the default branch". That leaves two
  # orders, and only one of them is safe. Merging with the dispatch triggers
  # live would put four never-executed jobs on the very next production mono
  # push, and a broken one would show as four red legs on every dispatch until
  # someone noticed. Merging manual-only registers the workflow so it can be
  # run deliberately, against a branch of our choosing, with no production
  # traffic touching it.
  #
  # Restore these two lines in the follow-up:
  # repository_dispatch:
  #   types:
  #     - mono-push
  #     - mono-merge-request

  # Allow manual triggering
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      gitlab_branch:
        description: 'seaweed-mono branch to test'
        required: false
        default: 'main'
      mono_sha:
        description: 'Exact seaweed-mono commit to test; defaults to the head of the branch above'
        required: false
        default: ''
      runner:
        description: 'Where to run: tp01 (self-hosted, no queue) or hosted (fallback when tp01 is down)'
        required: false
        type: choice
        default: hosted
        options: [tp01, hosted]
      measurement:
        description: 'Isolate this run from production: use a separate concurrency group so a real dispatch cannot cancel it'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  # head_ref is empty for repository_dispatch/workflow_dispatch, so key on the
  # dispatched mono ref (or the manual branch input) to actually dedupe runs.
  group: ${{ github.event.client_payload.ref || github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch || 'main' }}${{ inputs.measurement && '/measure' || '' }}/s3tables
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  s3tables-tests:
    name: S3 Tables (${{ matrix.suite }})
    runs-on: ${{ (inputs.runner || 'hosted') == 'tp01' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","tp01"]') || fromJSON('["ubuntu-22.04"]') }}
    timeout-minutes: 40
    strategy:
      # Report each suite independently; one failing must not hide the others.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - suite: maintenance
            dir: maintenance
            images: ''
          - suite: lifecycle
            dir: lifecycle
            images: 'python:3.11-slim'
          - suite: catalog_clickhouse
            dir: catalog_clickhouse
            images: 'clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.8 python:3.11-slim'
          - suite: catalog_olake
            dir: catalog_olake
            images: 'olakego/source-postgres:latest postgres:16 python:3.11-slim'

    steps:
    - name: Checkout artifactory repo
      uses: actions/checkout@v6
      with:
        persist-credentials: false

    - name: Runner housekeeping (self-hosted only)
      uses: ./.github/actions/runner-housekeeping

    - name: Link to seaweed-mono source
      if: github.event_name == 'repository_dispatch'
      uses: ./.github/actions/mono-source-link

    - name: Clone seaweed-mono (enterprise) source
      uses: ./.github/actions/clone-mono-source
      with:
        token: ${{ secrets.MONO_TOKEN }}
        branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch }}
        sha: ${{ inputs.mono_sha }}

    # Branches predating a suite have no directory. Skip that matrix leg rather
    # than failing, so the workflow stays usable on older refs.
    - name: Check for the suite
      id: check
      run: |
        present=false
        dir=seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/s3tables/${{ matrix.dir }}
        if [ -d "$dir" ]; then
          present=true
        else
          echo "::notice::Branch has no enterprise/test/s3tables/${{ matrix.dir }}; skipping."
        fi
        echo "present=$present" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    - name: Set up Go
      if: steps.check.outputs.present == 'true'
      uses: actions/setup-go@v6
      with:
        go-version-file: 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/go.mod'
        cache-dependency-path: 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/go.sum'

    # Mirror the registry only on hosted: this writes /etc/docker/daemon.json and
    # restarts the daemon under sudo, and tp01's runner account has no sudo at
    # all. On tp01 the images come from whatever the host already holds plus a
    # direct pull.
    - name: Configure Docker Hub mirror (hosted only)
      if: steps.check.outputs.present == 'true' && runner.environment == 'github-hosted'
      run: |
        echo '{"registry-mirrors": ["https://mirror.gcr.io"]}' | sudo tee /etc/docker/daemon.json
        sudo systemctl restart docker

    - name: Pre-pull images
      if: steps.check.outputs.present == 'true' && matrix.images != ''
      run: |
        pull() { for i in 1 2 3; do docker pull "$1" && return 0; sleep 15; done; return 1; }
        for image in ${{ matrix.images }}; do
          pull "$image"
        done

    # The suites locate the binary as weed/weed under the repo root or on PATH;
    # go install puts it on PATH via GOPATH/bin.
    - name: Install SeaweedFS
      if: steps.check.outputs.present == 'true'
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise
      run: go install -buildvcs=false ./weed

    - name: Run the suite
      if: steps.check.outputs.present == 'true'
      timeout-minutes: 35
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/s3tables/${{ matrix.dir }}
      run: |
        set -o pipefail
        echo "=== System information ==="
        uname -a
        free -h
        df -h
        go test -v -timeout 30m . 2>&1 | tee test-output.log || {
          echo "::error::enterprise/test/s3tables/${{ matrix.dir }} failed"
          exit 1
        }

    # A green job is not evidence the suite ran. These suites self-skip when
    # their environment is absent, so assert execution explicitly: at least one
    # top-level PASS, and no top-level SKIP. Without this the workflow would
    # report coverage it does not have, which is the failure this file exists to
    # prevent.
    - name: Assert the suite actually ran
      if: steps.check.outputs.present == 'true'
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/s3tables/${{ matrix.dir }}
      run: |
        log=test-output.log
        if [ ! -f "$log" ]; then
          echo "::error::no test-output.log; the suite did not run"
          exit 1
        fi
        passes=$(grep -c '^--- PASS' "$log" || true)
        skips=$(grep -c '^--- SKIP' "$log" || true)
        echo "top-level PASS=$passes SKIP=$skips"
        if [ "$skips" -gt 0 ]; then
          echo "::error::${{ matrix.suite }} skipped $skips top-level test(s) — the environment it needs was not provisioned, so this job proves nothing. Fix the environment rather than accepting the green."
          grep '^--- SKIP' "$log" | head -20
          exit 1
        fi
        if [ "$passes" -lt 1 ]; then
          echo "::error::${{ matrix.suite }} recorded no passing top-level test"
          exit 1
        fi

    - name: Show test output on failure
      if: failure() && steps.check.outputs.present == 'true'
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/s3tables/${{ matrix.dir }}
      run: |
        echo "=== Test output (tail) ==="
        if [ -f test-output.log ]; then
          tail -200 test-output.log
        fi
        echo "=== Processes ==="
        ps aux | grep -E "(weed|docker)" | head -30 || true
        echo "=== Containers ==="
        docker ps -a | head -30 || true

    - name: Upload test logs on failure
      if: failure() && steps.check.outputs.present == 'true'
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: s3tables-${{ matrix.suite }}-logs
        path: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/s3tables/${{ matrix.dir }}/test-output.log
        retention-days: 3

name: "RDMA software (siw) Tests (seaweed-mono)"
run-name: ${{ github.workflow }}${{ github.event.client_payload.sha && format(' · mono:{0}', github.event.client_payload.sha) || '' }}

on:
  # Triggered by seaweed-mono push (repository_dispatch)
  repository_dispatch:
    types:
      - mono-push
      - mono-merge-request

  # Allow manual triggering
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      gitlab_branch:
        description: 'seaweed-mono branch to test'
        required: false
        default: 'main'
      runner:
        description: "Runner label: ubuntu-22.04 (hosted, default) or tp01 (self-hosted; siw link and device access are pre-provisioned, no sudo)"
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-22.04'

concurrency:
  # `inputs.*` is empty in the workflow-level concurrency context; read the dispatch
  # input through github.event (2026-09-18: a tp01 dispatch cancelled another
  # branch's pending tp01 run because cancel-in-progress evaluated true).
  # head_ref is empty for repository_dispatch/workflow_dispatch, so key on the
  # dispatched mono ref (or the manual branch input) to actually dedupe runs.
  # One group per dispatched ref on every runner: GitHub keeps only ONE pending run per
  # group and cancels the older pending one, so a shared self-hosted group cancelled
  # other branches' queued tp01 runs (2026-09-18). Parallel tp01 runs share siw0; the
  # two tp01 runners bound the parallelism.
  # D-38 (2026-09-18): the serialisation added here rested on a wrong reading and is
  # withdrawn. All three restart-fence failures ran on the M-5.4d D2 line, never on the
  # tip; the cause is a client feature offer that puts the same-build server into
  # registration-only mode, so an ordinary read returns zero bytes. Control on one
  # runner, strictly sequential: candidate 3/3 red, tip 3/3 byte-exact. Concurrency was
  # never involved, so self-hosted runs group per dispatched ref like hosted ones.
  group: ${{ format('{0}/rdma-softroce-tests/{1}', github.event.client_payload.ref || github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch || 'main', github.event.inputs.runner || 'hosted') }}
  # Never cancel: with a self-hosted runner the group is shared across branches and an
  # expression here still cancelled the previous run (2026-09-18, runs 35308538083 and
  # 35308730850). Superseded hosted runs of one branch now queue instead of cancelling.
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Fast gate: the enterprise/rust workspace builds and its unit tests pass with
  # RDMA OFF (the default, macOS-buildable path). No SoftRoCE required.
  rdma-off-build:
    name: RDMA-off build + unit tests
    runs-on: ${{ github.event.inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-22.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 20

    steps:
      - name: Checkout artifactory repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Link to seaweed-mono source
        if: github.event_name == 'repository_dispatch'
        uses: ./.github/actions/mono-source-link

      - name: Clone seaweed-mono (enterprise) source
        uses: ./.github/actions/clone-mono-source
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.MONO_TOKEN }}
          branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch }}

      - name: Install protobuf compiler
        if: runner.environment == 'github-hosted'
        run: $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/apt-retry.sh update && $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/apt-retry.sh install -y protobuf-compiler

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Cache cargo registry and target
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust/target
          key: rust-rdma-${{ hashFiles('seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            rust-rdma-

      # Lib/bin build pulls no dev-deps, so the volume-server `rdma` feature and
      # rdma-sys are never compiled here — this stays a pure RDMA-off check.
      - name: Build enterprise/rust workspace (no RDMA)
        run: cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust && cargo build --workspace

      # The shipped volume server's RDMA-off runtime contract: every control-plane
      # RPC must degrade (prepare ok=false / commit Unimplemented / finish ok) so
      # the VFS client falls back to HTTP. Gated cfg(not(rdma)). seaweed-volume has
      # no rdma-sys dependency, so this builds without libibverbs (unlike the
      # enterprise/rust workspace, whose dev-deps drag in rdma-sys under `cargo
      # test` — those unit tests run on the SoftRoCE job below instead).
      - name: Shipped volume server RDMA-off contract test
        run: cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume && cargo test --features test-support --test rdma_disabled_contract


  # Full-wire RDMA datapath over software RDMA (siw): the read + write e2e tests
  # drive a real volume server + gRPC + one-sided RDMA. Needs the siw kernel
  # module and root for verbs/rdma_cm.
  rdma-softroce-e2e:
    name: software RDMA e2e (read + staged write)
    runs-on: ${{ github.event.inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-22.04' }}
    timeout-minutes: 40

    steps:
      # The stock ubuntu-22.04 runner ships only ~14 GB free on /, but this job
      # compiles two debug Rust target dirs (enterprise/rust + seaweed-volume)
      # plus a dozen --no-run e2e test binaries, which overflowed the disk
      # ("No space left on device"). Reclaim the tens of GB of preinstalled
      # toolchains this job never touches before building.
      - name: Free up disk space
        if: runner.environment == 'github-hosted'
        run: |
          set -x
          df -h /
          sudo rm -rf \
            /usr/local/lib/android \
            /usr/share/dotnet \
            /opt/ghc \
            /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL \
            /usr/local/share/boost \
            /usr/lib/jvm || true
          sudo docker image prune --all --force || true
          df -h /

      - name: Checkout artifactory repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Clone seaweed-mono (enterprise) source
        uses: ./.github/actions/clone-mono-source
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.MONO_TOKEN }}
          branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch }}

      # Build deps: protoc (tonic-build), clang/libclang (rdma-sys bindgen),
      # ibverbs/rdmacm headers. Runtime: rdma-core (`rdma`), ibverbs-utils
      # (`ibv_devices`) and the userspace siw provider, libsiw (ibverbs-providers).
      - name: Install build + RDMA userspace deps
        if: runner.environment == 'github-hosted'
        run: |
          $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/apt-retry.sh update
          $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/apt-retry.sh install -y \
            protobuf-compiler clang libclang-dev \
            libibverbs-dev librdmacm-dev rdma-core ibverbs-providers ibverbs-utils

      - name: Bring up software RDMA (siw / Soft-iWARP)
        if: runner.environment == 'github-hosted'
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          # GitHub's ubuntu-22.04 runners boot the linux-azure kernel, which ships
          # siw (Soft-iWARP) but NOT rdma_rxe (SoftRoCE) in modules-extra. siw drives
          # the same RC verbs + rdma_cm (RDMA_PS_TCP) path these one-sided read/write
          # e2e tests use, so it is a drop-in software RDMA transport here.
          # A miss here is expected and tolerated, so no retries -- but still go
          # through the wrapper, which bounds the attempt if the mirror hangs.
          APT_RETRY_ATTEMPTS=1 $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/apt-retry.sh \
            install -y "linux-modules-extra-$(uname -r)" || \
            echo "linux-modules-extra not available; relying on in-tree siw"
          sudo modprobe siw || { echo "::error::siw module unavailable on $(uname -r)"; exit 1; }
          # Give siw its own dummy netdev with a private IP. eth0 also carries
          # Azure's hardware RDMA device (mana_0), which hijacks rdma_cm IP->device
          # resolution and fails create_ep with ENODEV; and rdma_cm refuses to bind
          # a device to a loopback (127.0.0.1) address ("no device context"). A
          # private IP on a dummy interface maps only to siw0 and is a real
          # (non-loopback) device context; same-host connects deliver locally.
          sudo modprobe dummy || true
          SOFT_RDMA_NETDEV="${SOFT_RDMA_NETDEV:-rdma-ci-dummy0}"
          SOFT_RDMA_IP="${SOFT_RDMA_IP:-198.51.100.1}"
          sudo ip link add "$SOFT_RDMA_NETDEV" type dummy
          sudo ip addr add "$SOFT_RDMA_IP/24" dev "$SOFT_RDMA_NETDEV"
          sudo ip link set "$SOFT_RDMA_NETDEV" up
          sudo rdma link add siw0 type siw netdev "$SOFT_RDMA_NETDEV"
          rdma link
          ibv_devices
          # Fail loudly (not silently skip) if siw didn't come up on this kernel.
          # `rdma link` names the link "<dev>/<port>" (e.g. siw0/1), so match by device.
          rdma link | grep -q 'siw0' || { echo "::error::software RDMA siw0 unavailable on this runner kernel"; exit 1; }
          # The e2e tests read the target IP from RXE_IP (kept as the test's contract).
          echo "RXE_IP=$SOFT_RDMA_IP" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Self-hosted runners carry a persistent siw link (systemd siw-ci.service:
      # siw0 on dummy netdev siwci, 198.51.100.1/24) and the runner user is in
      # the rdma group with LimitMEMLOCK=infinity, so no sudo is needed. Fail
      # loudly if the link is not there rather than silently testing nothing.
      - name: Verify pre-provisioned software RDMA (self-hosted)
        if: runner.environment != 'github-hosted'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rdma link | grep -q '^link siw0/' || { echo "::error::siw0 not provisioned on $(hostname); see siw-ci.service"; exit 1; }
          ibv_devices | grep -q siw0 || { echo "::error::siw0 not visible to $(id -un); check the rdma group / udev rules"; exit 1; }
          echo "RXE_IP=${SOFT_RDMA_IP:-198.51.100.1}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      # Caches both the enterprise/rust workspace and the separate shipped
      # volume-server (enterprise/seaweed-volume) target dirs — this job builds
      # both — keyed off both lockfiles so a change to either invalidates.
      - name: Cache cargo registry and target
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust/target
            seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume/target
          key: rust-rdma-${{ hashFiles('seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust/Cargo.lock', 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            rust-rdma-

      # Explicitly compile the shipped volume server (enterprise/seaweed-volume)
      # with RDMA so a compile error surfaces here, not buried in the e2e build.
      # Built in its own workspace, where its lockfile is authoritative.
      - name: Build shipped volume server (RDMA)
        run: |
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume
          cargo build --features rdma

      # The shipped volume server's lib unit tests cover the RDMA gates (deleted/
      # TTL needle rejection, EC shard path/locate/needle-info) and runtime ABA
      # detection — pure logic, no device — so run them with rdma on (no sudo).
      - name: Shipped volume server unit tests (RDMA on)
        run: |
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume
          cargo test --features rdma --lib

      # RDMA modularisation crates (rdma/dev, milestone 2 onwards): the portable
      # core (mock provider, boundary) and the verbs provider's loopback over the
      # siw device set up above. Skipped, not failed, on a tree that predates them.
      - name: sw-rdma-core + provider-verbs (soft-RDMA loopback)
        run: |
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust
          if [ -d sw-rdma-core ] && [ -d sw-rdma-provider-verbs ]; then
            cargo test -p seaweedfs-sw-rdma-core
            cargo test -p seaweedfs-sw-rdma-provider-verbs --features real-rdma,test-support
          else
            echo "sw-rdma-core / sw-rdma-provider-verbs not in this tree — skipped"
          fi

      # Boundary guard for the provider abstraction: generic verbs / rdma_cm and
      # vendor (mlx5dv, libfabric) symbols may only appear inside provider crates
      # and the EFA C shim. Strict once the core crate exists in the tree.
      - name: Rust RDMA boundary guard
        run: |
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust
          if [ ! -d sw-rdma-core ]; then echo "pre-modularisation tree — guard skipped"; exit 0; fi
          rc=0
          check() { # $1 = regex, $2 = allowed-path regex, $3 = label
            hits=$(grep -rnE --include='*.rs' "$1" . | grep -vE '/(vendor|target)/' | grep -vE ':[0-9]+:\s*//' | grep -vE "$2" || true)
            if [ -n "$hits" ]; then echo "::error::$3 outside its provider:"; echo "$hits" | head -20; rc=1; fi
          }
          check '\b(ibv_|rdma_cm_|rdma_create_id)' '^\./(sw-rdma-provider-verbs|sw-rdma-provider-mlx5|sw-rdma-provider-efa)/|/tests/boundary\.rs' 'generic verbs/rdma_cm symbol'
          check '\b(mlx5dv_|wr_set_dc_addr)' '^\./sw-rdma-provider-mlx5/|/tests/boundary\.rs' 'mlx5 symbol'
          check '\bfi_[a-z_]+\(' '^\./(sw-rdma-provider-efa|sw-rdma/src/efa)|/efa_shim|/tests/boundary\.rs' 'libfabric symbol'
          exit $rc

      # sw-rdma-vfs lib unit tests (e.g. parse_fid length bounds). cargo test pulls
      # rdma-sys via dev-deps, so these run on this job (libibverbs installed),
      # reusing the real-rdma build from the e2e step above.
      - name: sw-rdma-vfs unit tests (real-rdma)
        run: cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust && cargo test -p seaweedfs-sw-rdma-vfs --features real-rdma --lib

      # Build the shared RDMA loader/object surface with real RDMA enabled. This
      # catches libibverbs/rdma_cm link breakage in the code used by object/S3
      # coordinator paths without making a hardware performance claim.
      - name: Build RDMA loader/object clients (real-rdma)
        run: |
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust
          cargo test -p seaweedfs-sw-rdma-loader -p seaweedfs-sw-rdma-object --features real-rdma --lib --no-run
          cargo build -p seaweedfs-sw-rdma-object --features real-rdma --bins

      # Build every sw-rdma-vfs/tests/rdma_*_e2e.rs present on the dispatched mono
      # branch (read, staged write, replication, volume move, ...), so adding a
      # test on a branch needs no workflow change and main stays green.
      - name: Build RDMA e2e tests (real-rdma)
        run: |
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust
          TESTS=""
          for f in sw-rdma-vfs/tests/rdma_*_e2e.rs; do
            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
            TESTS="$TESTS --test $(basename "$f" .rs)"
          done
          echo "building e2e tests:$TESTS"
          cargo test -p seaweedfs-sw-rdma-vfs --features real-rdma $TESTS --no-run

      - name: Run RDMA e2e over software RDMA (sudo)
        env:
          RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
        run: |
          set -uxo pipefail
          # Verbs/rdma_cm need root only on hosted runners; self-hosted runners
          # pre-provision device access and memlock for the runner user.
          SUDO=sudo; [ "${RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT:-}" = github-hosted ] || SUDO=""
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust
          rc=0
          for f in sw-rdma-vfs/tests/rdma_*_e2e.rs; do
            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
            t=$(basename "$f" .rs)
            BIN=$(ls -t target/debug/deps/${t}-* 2>/dev/null | grep -v '\.d$' | head -n1 || true)
            if [ -z "$BIN" ]; then echo "::error::test binary for $t not found"; exit 1; fi
            echo "== running $t :: $BIN =="
            # Verbs/rdma_cm need root; raise memlock so reg_mr can pin MRs.
            if ! $SUDO env "RXE_IP=$RXE_IP" "RUST_BACKTRACE=$RUST_BACKTRACE" \
              bash -c "ulimit -l unlimited && '$BIN' --nocapture --test-threads=1"; then
              echo "::error::$t failed"; rc=1
            fi
          done
          exit $rc

      # Optional object/loader e2e tests. These are auto-discovered from the
      # dispatched seaweed-mono branch, so adding an RDMA object correctness test
      # in mono next month does not require another artifactory workflow change.
      - name: Build object/loader RDMA e2e tests (real-rdma)
        run: |
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust
          for root in sw-rdma-loader sw-rdma-object; do
            TESTS=""
            for f in "$root"/tests/rdma_*_e2e.rs; do
              [ -e "$f" ] || continue
              TESTS="$TESTS --test $(basename "$f" .rs)"
            done
            [ -n "$TESTS" ] || { echo "no $root RDMA e2e tests"; continue; }
            echo "building $root e2e tests:$TESTS"
            cargo test -p seaweedfs-${root} --features real-rdma $TESTS --no-run
          done

      - name: Run object/loader RDMA e2e over software RDMA (sudo)
        env:
          RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
        run: |
          set -uxo pipefail
          # Verbs/rdma_cm need root only on hosted runners; self-hosted runners
          # pre-provision device access and memlock for the runner user.
          SUDO=sudo; [ "${RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT:-}" = github-hosted ] || SUDO=""
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust
          rc=0
          for root in sw-rdma-loader sw-rdma-object; do
            for f in "$root"/tests/rdma_*_e2e.rs; do
              [ -e "$f" ] || continue
              t=$(basename "$f" .rs)
              BIN=$(ls -t target/debug/deps/${t}-* 2>/dev/null | grep -v '\.d$' | head -n1 || true)
              if [ -z "$BIN" ]; then echo "::error::test binary for $root/$t not found"; exit 1; fi
              echo "== running $root/$t :: $BIN =="
              if ! $SUDO env "RXE_IP=$RXE_IP" "RUST_BACKTRACE=$RUST_BACKTRACE" \
                bash -c "ulimit -l unlimited && '$BIN' --nocapture --test-threads=1"; then
                echo "::error::$root/$t failed"; rc=1
              fi
            done
          done
          exit $rc

      # The shipped volume server (enterprise/seaweed-volume) is a separate crate
      # with its own RDMA e2e tests (volume move over one-sided RDMA), built with
      # the `rdma` + `test-support` features. Auto-discovered like the sw-rdma-vfs
      # set so adding a test on a branch needs no workflow change.
      - name: Build shipped volume server RDMA e2e tests (rdma)
        run: |
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume
          TESTS=""
          for f in tests/rdma_*_e2e.rs; do
            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
            TESTS="$TESTS --test $(basename "$f" .rs)"
          done
          if [ -z "$TESTS" ]; then echo "no shipped-volume RDMA e2e tests"; exit 0; fi
          echo "building shipped-volume e2e tests:$TESTS"
          cargo test --features rdma,test-support $TESTS --no-run

      - name: Run shipped volume server RDMA e2e over software RDMA (sudo)
        env:
          RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
        run: |
          set -uxo pipefail
          # Verbs/rdma_cm need root only on hosted runners; self-hosted runners
          # pre-provision device access and memlock for the runner user.
          SUDO=sudo; [ "${RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT:-}" = github-hosted ] || SUDO=""
          cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume
          rc=0
          for f in tests/rdma_*_e2e.rs; do
            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
            t=$(basename "$f" .rs)
            BIN=$(ls -t target/debug/deps/${t}-* 2>/dev/null | grep -v '\.d$' | head -n1 || true)
            if [ -z "$BIN" ]; then echo "::error::test binary for $t not found"; exit 1; fi
            echo "== running $t :: $BIN =="
            # Verbs/rdma_cm need root; raise memlock so reg_mr can pin MRs.
            if ! $SUDO env "RXE_IP=$RXE_IP" "RUST_BACKTRACE=$RUST_BACKTRACE" \
              bash -c "ulimit -l unlimited && '$BIN' --nocapture --test-threads=1"; then
              echo "::error::$t failed"; rc=1
            fi
          done
          exit $rc

      - name: Test summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          # Derive the listed tests from the same glob the build/run steps use, so
          # a newly added rdma_*_e2e.rs shows up here with no workflow change.
          vfs=$(cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust 2>/dev/null && for f in sw-rdma-vfs/tests/rdma_*_e2e.rs; do [ -e "$f" ] && basename "$f" .rs; done | paste -sd, -)
          loader=$(cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust 2>/dev/null && for f in sw-rdma-loader/tests/rdma_*_e2e.rs; do [ -e "$f" ] && basename "$f" .rs; done | paste -sd, -)
          object=$(cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/rust 2>/dev/null && for f in sw-rdma-object/tests/rdma_*_e2e.rs; do [ -e "$f" ] && basename "$f" .rs; done | paste -sd, -)
          vol=$(cd seaweedfs-source/enterprise/seaweed-volume 2>/dev/null && for f in tests/rdma_*_e2e.rs; do [ -e "$f" ] && basename "$f" .rs; done | paste -sd, -)
          {
            echo "## RDMA software (siw) e2e summary"
            echo "- Layer: Soft-iWARP (siw) over the runner NIC"
            echo "- sw-rdma-loader (real-rdma): ${loader:-none}"
            echo "- sw-rdma-object (real-rdma): ${object:-none}"
            echo "- sw-rdma-vfs (real-rdma): ${vfs:-none}"
            echo "- seaweed-volume (rdma,test-support): ${vol:-none}"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: "Kafka Gateway Tests (seaweed-mono)"
# The dispatch inputs ride in the run name so the runner watchdog
# (runner-watchdog.yml) can cancel a run stuck on an offline tp01 and
# re-dispatch it on hosted with the same inputs. Keep the fields parseable:
# mono:<sha> branch:<ref> runner:<tp01|hosted>.
run-name: ${{ github.workflow }}${{ (github.event.client_payload.sha || inputs.mono_sha) && format(' · mono:{0}', github.event.client_payload.sha || inputs.mono_sha) || '' }} · branch:${{ github.event.client_payload.ref || inputs.gitlab_branch || 'main' }} · runner:${{ inputs.runner || 'hosted' }}

on:
  # Triggered by seaweed-mono push (repository_dispatch)
  repository_dispatch:
    types:
      - mono-push
      - mono-merge-request

  # Allow manual triggering
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      gitlab_branch:
        description: 'seaweed-mono branch to test'
        required: false
        default: 'main'
      mono_sha:
        description: 'Exact seaweed-mono commit to test; defaults to the head of the branch above'
        required: false
        default: ''
      runner:
        description: 'Where to run: tp01 (self-hosted, no queue) or hosted (fallback when tp01 is down)'
        required: false
        type: choice
        default: hosted
        options: [tp01, hosted]
      measurement:
        description: 'Isolate this run from production: use a separate concurrency group so a real dispatch cannot cancel it'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  # head_ref is empty for repository_dispatch/workflow_dispatch, so key on the
  # dispatched mono ref (or the manual branch input) to actually dedupe runs.
  group: ${{ github.event.client_payload.ref || github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch || 'main' }}${{ inputs.measurement && '/measure' || '' }}/kafka-tests

    # alike.

    steps:
    - name: Checkout artifactory repo
      uses: actions/checkout@v6

    - name: Runner housekeeping (self-hosted only)
      uses: ./.github/actions/runner-housekeeping

    - name: Clone seaweed-mono (enterprise) source
      uses: ./.github/actions/clone-mono-source
      with:
        token: ${{ secrets.MONO_TOKEN }}
        branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch }}
        sha: ${{ inputs.mono_sha }}

    - name: Set up Go 1.x
      uses: actions/setup-go@v6
      with:
        go-version-file: 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/go.mod'
        cache: true
        cache-dependency-path: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/kafka/**/go.sum
      id: go

    - name: Get dependencies
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/kafka
      run: |

    - name: Run Integration Tests

      run: |

        ulimit -u 200 || echo "Warning: Could not set process limit"

      env:
        GOMAXPROCS: 2

  kafka-e2e-tests:
    name: Kafka End-to-End Tests (with SMQ)
    # tp01 exports a per-instance port band (CI_MASTER_PORT etc., see the tp01
    # runbook) so two different instances can run this suite's fixed ports at
    # once without colliding; the concurrency key below only needs to stop a
    # literal retry of the SAME run+job+shard piling up, on tp01 or hosted
    # alike.
    concurrency:
      group: ${{ format('{0}-{1}-kafka-e2e-tests-{2}', inputs.runner || 'hosted', github.run_id, strategy.job-index) }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ${{ (inputs.runner || 'hosted') == 'tp01' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","tp01"]') || fromJSON('["ubuntu-latest"]') }}
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        container-id: [e2e-1]
    env:
      GOMAXPROCS: 2
      CGO_ENABLED: 0
      KAFKA_E2E_ISOLATION: "true"
      CONTAINER_ID: ${{ matrix.container-id }}
    steps:
    - name: Checkout artifactory repo
      uses: actions/checkout@v6

    - name: Runner housekeeping (self-hosted only)
      uses: ./.github/actions/runner-housekeeping

    - name: Clone seaweed-mono (enterprise) source
      uses: ./.github/actions/clone-mono-source
      with:
        token: ${{ secrets.MONO_TOKEN }}
        branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.gitlab_branch }}
        sha: ${{ inputs.mono_sha }}

    - name: Set up Go 1.x
      uses: actions/setup-go@v6
      with:
        go-version-file: 'seaweedfs-source/enterprise/go.mod'
        cache: true
        cache-dependency-path: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/kafka/**/go.sum
      id: go

    - name: Warm Go module cache
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise
      run: |
        # Warm cache for root module
        go mod download || true
        # Warm cache for kafka test module
        cd test/kafka
        go mod download || true

    - name: Get dependencies
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/kafka
      run: |
        # Use go mod download with timeout to prevent hanging
        timeout 90s go mod download || echo "Warning: Dependency download timed out, continuing with cached modules"
        go mod tidy

    - name: Build and start SeaweedFS MQ
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise
      run: |
        set -e
        # Build to a per-job bin directory, not /usr/local/bin: that is a single
        # shared system path, and two jobs on two different runner instances
        # building to it at once race and one gets "permission denied" mid-write
        # (found live on this host once tp01-2 could genuinely run alongside tp01).
        # $RUNNER_TEMP is unique per job by construction, so this also cannot leak
        # one run's binary into the next on a persistent runner.
        mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin"
        export PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/bin:$PATH"
        go build -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin/weed" ./weed
        # Start SeaweedFS components with MQ brokers
        export WEED_DATA_DIR=/tmp/seaweedfs-e2e-$RANDOM
        mkdir -p "$WEED_DATA_DIR"

        # Start SeaweedFS server (master, volume, filer) with consistent IP advertising
        # CI_MASTER_PORT/CI_VOLUME_PORT/CI_FILER_PORT come from the tp01 runner hook
        # (absent on hosted, so the :- defaults below are hosted's actual behaviour).
        # gRPC and metrics are not exported directly: gRPC is SeaweedFS's own
        # port+10000 convention, and metrics only needs to avoid the SAME collision
        # as the others, so it is derived from the same instance band.
        CI_MASTER_GRPC_PORT=$(( ${CI_MASTER_PORT:-9333} + 10000 ))
        CI_METRICS_PORT="${CI_PORT_BASE:+$((CI_PORT_BASE + 50))}"
        CI_METRICS_PORT="${CI_METRICS_PORT:-9325}"
        nohup weed -v 1 server \
          -ip="127.0.0.1" \
          -ip.bind="0.0.0.0" \
          -dir="$WEED_DATA_DIR" \
          -master.raftHashicorp \
          -master.port=${CI_MASTER_PORT:-9333} \
          -volume.port=${CI_VOLUME_PORT:-8081} \
          -filer.port=${CI_FILER_PORT:-8888} \
          -filer=true \
          -metricsPort=${CI_METRICS_PORT} \
          -master.peers=none \
          > "$RUNNER_TEMP/weed-server.log" 2>&1 &

        # Wait for master to be ready
        for i in $(seq 1 30); do
          if curl -s http://127.0.0.1:${CI_MASTER_PORT:-9333}/cluster/status >/dev/null; then
            echo "SeaweedFS master HTTP is up"; break
          fi
          echo "Waiting for SeaweedFS master HTTP... ($i/30)"; sleep 1
        done

        # Wait for master gRPC to be ready (this is what broker discovery uses)
        echo "Waiting for master gRPC port..."
        for i in $(seq 1 30); do
          if nc -z 127.0.0.1 $CI_MASTER_GRPC_PORT 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "SeaweedFS master gRPC is up (port $CI_MASTER_GRPC_PORT)"
            break
          fi
          echo "  Waiting for master gRPC... ($i/30)"; sleep 1
        done

        # Give server time to initialize all components including gRPC services
        echo "Waiting for SeaweedFS components to initialize..."
        sleep 15

        # Additional wait specifically for gRPC services to be ready for streaming
        echo "Allowing extra time for master gRPC streaming services to initialize..."
        sleep 10

        # Start MQ broker with maximum verbosity for debugging
        echo "Starting MQ broker..."
        CI_BROKER_PORT="${CI_PORT_BASE:+$((CI_PORT_BASE + 60))}"
        CI_BROKER_PORT="${CI_BROKER_PORT:-17777}"
        nohup weed -v 3 mq.broker \
          -master="127.0.0.1:${CI_MASTER_PORT:-9333}" \
          -ip="127.0.0.1" \
          -port=$CI_BROKER_PORT \
          -logFlushInterval=0 \
          > "$RUNNER_TEMP/weed-mq-broker.log" 2>&1 &

        # Wait for broker to be ready with better error reporting
        sleep 15
        broker_ready=false
        for i in $(seq 1 20); do
          if nc -z 127.0.0.1 $CI_BROKER_PORT 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "SeaweedFS MQ broker is up"
            broker_ready=true
            break
          fi
          echo "Waiting for MQ broker... ($i/20)"; sleep 1
        done

        # Give broker additional time to register with master
        if [ "$broker_ready" = true ]; then
          echo "Allowing broker to register with master..."
          sleep 30
          echo "Cluster status after broker registration:"
          curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:${CI_MASTER_PORT:-9333}/cluster/status" || echo "Could not check cluster status"
        fi

        # Check if broker failed to start and show logs
        if [ "$broker_ready" = false ]; then
          echo "ERROR: MQ broker failed to start. Broker logs:"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/weed-mq-broker.log" || echo "No broker logs found"
          echo "Server logs:"
          tail -20 "$RUNNER_TEMP/weed-server.log" || echo "No server logs found"
          exit 1
        fi

    - name: Run End-to-End Tests
      working-directory: seaweedfs-source/enterprise/test/kafka
      run: |
        # Higher limits for E2E tests
        ulimit -n 1024 || echo "Warning: Could not set file descriptor limit"
        ulimit -u 200 || echo "Warning: Could not set process limit"

        # Allow additional time for all background processes to settle
        echo "Allowing additional settlement time for SeaweedFS ecosystem..."
        sleep 15

        # Run tests and capture result
        if ! go test -v -timeout 180s ./e2e/...; then
          echo "========================================="
          echo "Tests failed! Showing debug information:"
          echo "========================================="
          echo "Server logs (last 50 lines):"
          tail -50 "$RUNNER_TEMP/weed-server.log" || echo "No server logs"
          echo "========================================="
          echo "Broker logs (last 50 lines):"
          tail -50 "$RUNNER_TEMP/weed-mq-broker.log" || echo "No broker logs"
          echo "========================================="
          exit 1
        fi
      env:
        GOMAXPROCS: 2
        SEAWEEDFS_MASTERS: 127.0.0.1:${{ env.CI_MASTER_PORT || '9333' }}

    - name: Upload test logs on failure
      if: failure()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: kafka-e2e-logs-${{ env.COMMIT_SHA }}
        path: |
          ${{ runner.temp }}/weed-server.log

        retention-days: 3

# RDMA Lab CI

This is the M01/M02 hardware gate for RDMA work in `seaweed-mono`.

GitHub Actions already runs the software RDMA gate with `siw`. That catches
build/link and basic verbs regressions. This runner is different: it uses the
real M01/M02 RoCE lab and should be used before opening or updating RDMA PRs
that make performance or hardware-behavior claims.

## Current Shape

- M01: client / runner host.
- M02: Seaweed master, filer, and RDMA-enabled Rust volume host.
- Buildkite provides the web UI and GitHub trigger.
- `run-mono-rdma-lab.sh` can also be run manually on M01.

The first supported profile is `unified`. It runs the mono
`sw-rdma-loader/tests/lab/unified-rdma-gate` scripts and checks the current
object/loader path:

- one `enterprise/seaweed-volume` server;
- object and VFS access to the same namespace;
- RC push, RC pull, and optional DC push rows;
- SHA/byte correctness;
- benchmark lines for the active rows.

## Install on M01

1. Install a Buildkite agent on M01.
2. Register it with queue tag `m01-rdma`.
3. Give it SSH access to M02 as the lab user.
4. Put any private GitHub token or SSH key setup in the agent environment, not
   in this repo.
5. Create a Buildkite pipeline that points at this repo and uses
   `.buildkite/rdma-lab.yml`.

The same runner works without Buildkite:

```bash
bash rdma-lab-ci/run-mono-rdma-lab.sh \
  --repo https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweed-mono.git \
  --ref main \
  --profile unified
```

For a PR branch:

```bash
bash rdma-lab-ci/run-mono-rdma-lab.sh \
  --ref rdma/transfer-context-v2 \
  --profile unified
```

## Local Artifact Web UI

For a simple web view on M01, run `serve-artifacts.py` behind Basic Auth:

```bash
RDMA_CI_USER=rdma \
RDMA_CI_PASSWORD='change-me' \
RDMA_CI_ROOT=/opt/rdma-lab-ci/artifacts \
RDMA_CI_PORT=8091 \
python3 rdma-lab-ci/serve-artifacts.py
```

Open:

```text
http://M01:8091/
```

Each run directory contains `index.html`, `run.log`, `provenance.txt`, and
`summary.env`.

## Pass Criteria

The run must print:

- `UNIFIED_SINGLE_VOLUME_SERVER_OK`
- `UNIFIED_OBJECT_TO_VFS_SHA_MATCH`
- `UNIFIED_VFS_TO_OBJECT_SHA_MATCH`
- `UNIFIED_S3_LOADER_MATRIX_DONE`
- `UNIFIED_VFS_READ_MATRIX_DONE`
- `UNIFIED_RDMA_GATE_PASS`

For the current object hot path, the PR evidence should also record:

- RC push throughput for 20MiB/c32 and 128MiB/c32;
- RC pull throughput for 20MiB/c32 and 128MiB/c32;
- DC push throughput when the `mlx5-dc` feature is enabled;
- SHA match for every claimed row;
- explicit fallback/unsupported status for rows that are not implemented.

Do not claim a backend row from this CI unless the row is printed by the gate
and the SHA check passes.

## Outputs

Each run writes to `rdma-lab-runs/<timestamp>-<ref>-<profile>/`:

- `provenance.txt`
- `run.log`
- `summary.env`

Buildkite uploads that directory as an artifact. For manual runs, serve the
directory with any static file server if a simple web view is needed.

## Notes

This runner is intentionally thin. It does not reimplement the RDMA tests.
The canonical test logic lives in `seaweed-mono` next to the code it validates.

ROOT=pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
    root=pathlib.Path(temporary); tools=root/'bin';tools.mkdir()
    product=root/'product';product.mkdir()
    pin='a'*40
    tests=product/'enterprise/rust/tests';tests.mkdir(parents=True)

    for name in names:(tests/name).write_text('')

    (tools/'python3').write_text('''#!/bin/sh
case "$1" in
 *s4_error*) echo 'S4-ERROR-CLASSIFICATION-SELF-TEST PASS';;
 *lease_explicit*) echo 'LEF-SELF-TEST PASS';;
 *) exit 99;;
esac
[ "$MODE" != missing_receipt ] || exit 0
[ "$MODE" != nonzero ] || exit 7
''')
    for tool in tools.iterdir():tool.chmod(0o755)
    env=dict(os.environ,PATH=str(tools)+':'+os.environ['PATH'],ACTUAL_PIN=pin)
    def run(mode,expected,pin_arg=pin,actual=pin):
        env.update(MODE=mode,ACTUAL_PIN=actual)
        # Missing-receipt control deletes output in the real subprocess seam.
        if mode=='missing_receipt':
            (tools/'python3').write_text('#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n')
            (tools/'python3').chmod(0o755)
        r=subprocess.run(['bash',str(ROOT/'rdma-lab-ci/contract-self-tests.sh'),str(product),pin_arg],env=env,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10)
        print('F3-CONTROL',mode,'rc='+str(r.returncode),flush=True)
        assert (r.returncode==0)==expected,r.stdout+r.stderr
        if mode in ('nonzero','missing_receipt'):
            assert r.stdout.count('CONTRACT-VERDICT')==2
            assert 'failed=1' in r.stdout
    run('positive',True)
    run('nonzero',False)
    run('mismatch',False,actual='b'*40)
    run('detached',False,pin_arg='HEAD')
    run('missing_receipt',False)
    # One contract missing = broken RDMA tree: still fails closed.
    (tests/names[1]).unlink()

    (tests/names[0]).unlink()
    r=subprocess.run(['bash',str(ROOT/'rdma-lab-ci/contract-self-tests.sh'),str(product),pin],env=env,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10)
    print('F3-CONTROL not_applicable rc='+str(r.returncode),flush=True)
    assert r.returncode==0 and 'status=NOT_APPLICABLE' in r.stdout and 'CONTRACT-VERDICT' not in r.stdout,r.stdout+r.stderr
